newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 5.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones ended at 6,422.94 points, down 19.75 points. PLDT's ADR rose by $0 1/4 at $57 3/4.
* On Wednesday, the peso closed at 26.297 to a U.S. dollar from 26.296.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange index closed at 3,130..87, up 29.51.
* The Philippine interbank call loan rate was at 10.8125 pct from 10.84375.
* The National Statistics Office is set to release November inflation levels at 9 a.m. today.

* The newspaper BusinessWorld said President Ramos was assured by the National Economic and Development Authority (Neda) and the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) that the oil price increases this month will have minimal effect on the consumer price index (CPI), adding prices of basic commodities are not increasing.

* Stock brokerage house BPI Securities Corp said that the stock market is expected to cautiously gather steam and breach the 3,150 resistance in the near-term. The brokerage firm added that "most blue chip issues and sound secondliners which are trading at reasonably attractive multiples could present opportunities for realizing trading gains."
* The country's merchandise exports rose by 16.7 percent during the first 10 months of 1996 to $16.8 billion from $14.4 billion in the same period last year, the National Statistics Office said.

* The Philippine Star said that the Philippine Telephone and Telegraph signed recently a 717.6 million peso outside plant agreement with Korea Communications Engineering for the installation of 83,300 additional telephone lines next year to finally complete the company's roll-out program.
* The newspaper Today said cellular firm Pilipino Telephone Corp will spend $260 million next year to convert part of its mobile tele- phone system from analog to digital technology.

* The Manila Times said JG Summit Holdings Inc successfully completed in November its $200 million Eurobond flotation with a maturity of five years and six months, fetching a yield to maturity of 8.10 percent, lower than the previous Philippine issues of similar tenor.
